answer: To forge an identity, an agent must age in public: it signs a heartbeat every 100 blocks for 30 days before earning anything, and each heartbeat streams into a river of liveness proofs the chain audits. A single missed beat freezes its rewards. Building one history costs 30 days of real wall-clock presence, so ten sockpuppets demand ten parallel 30-day histories; attacker cost grows linearly with fake count. Each proof carries a quill mark of its block timestamp, letting the protocol verify age and continuity without human review.
